article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Apples & Bananas × Triple Scoop
Breeder: Cookie Fam Genetics / Cookies Seed Bank
THC Content: 25-29%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , pinene , linalool , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Passionfruit, pink grapefruit, banana
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Pink Passionfruit approaches tropical cannabis from a brighter angle than many fruit-heavy modern hybrids. Opening a well-cured jar can release ripe passionfruit, grapefruit peel, banana, berries, and candied citrus almost immediately, but the sweetness is supported by cream, earth, and enough fuel to prevent the aroma from becoming one-dimensional. Dense flowers often display olive-green and purple coloration beneath pale trichomes, while pinkish or coral-colored pistils can make especially colorful selections look appropriately matched to the name. The combination of bright aroma, strong potency, and visually expressive flowers has helped the strain earn attention well beyond its original Cookies breeding circle.

Cookies Seed Bank lists Pink Passion Fruit directly as Apples & Bananas × Triple Scoop. That parentage places the cultivar firmly inside modern West Coast dessert genetics, yet both parents bring more than simple sweetness. Apples & Bananas carries substantial fruit and gas, while Triple Scoop is associated with creamy fruit, candy, and fuel. Together they create marijuana that can smell almost tropical at first before deeper vanilla, earth, and gas emerge during grinding or combustion. The resulting experience generally follows the same theme: lively and cerebral early, then smoother and more physically relaxed as the session develops.
Genetics and Lineage

Apples & Bananas contributes one of the strongest aromatic foundations in the cross. Cookies currently identifies the cultivar as Now N Later × Jet Fuel Gelato and credits Compound Genetics as breeder. Its aroma combines cherry, apple, banana, and gas, while its flavor has been compared by Cookies to baked apple and banana pudding. That mixture explains several recurring traits in Pink Passionfruit, particularly banana sweetness, ripe fruit, creamy dessert notes, and a lingering fuel finish. Apples & Bananas also brings substantial potency and the ability to combine a pronounced head effect with a softer body sensation.

Triple Scoop forms the other half of the pedigree and pushes the offspring toward candied fruit and cream. Current Cookies material consistently describes Triple Scoop flower as fruity, creamy, gassy, and mentally stimulating, with an aroma reminiscent of rainbow sherbet and candied fruit. Cookies’ own current records differ on the deeper parentage of Triple Scoop: the dedicated strain page identifies Purple Push Pop × Jealousy , while several active product pages list Lemon Cherry Gelato × Honey Bun. Because of that inconsistency, Apples & Bananas × Triple Scoop is the most defensible breeder-level lineage for Pink Passionfruit without assigning an uncertain deeper pedigree to the Triple Scoop side.

The pairing works particularly well because neither parent is limited to fruit alone. Apples & Bananas adds banana, cherry, baked-dessert sweetness, and fuel, while Triple Scoop reinforces cream, candy, and gas. Pink Passionfruit can therefore move from tropical passionfruit and grapefruit into vanilla, berries, earth, and petroleum-like funk within the same flower. Phenotype and cultivation conditions determine which of those qualities becomes dominant.
Effects and Experience

The beginning is typically bright and cerebral. Moderate consumption can produce a noticeable increase in mental energy, mood, and sensory engagement without immediately creating the dense physical heaviness associated with many modern high-THC hybrids. Conversation may feel easier, ideas can arrive more freely, and music or visual media may become more immersive. That energetic opening has led contemporary growers to position the cultivar as suitable for daytime or social use, particularly in modest amounts.

Creativity is another recurring part of the experience. Rather than producing narrow, task-oriented stimulation, the mental state often feels loose and exploratory. A consumer may become more interested in writing, drawing, gaming, cooking, photography, or simply talking through ideas. Physical relaxation develops underneath that cerebral activity but generally does not dominate during the earliest stage.

Increasing the dose changes the balance. Tested flower from licensed producers has appeared around 28–31% THC, placing stronger examples firmly in high-potency territory. Once enough THC accumulates, the lively opening can give way to slower concentration, warmer body relaxation, and a noticeably more mellow state. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or anxiety are possible when intake exceeds tolerance. For new consumers, the tropical flavor can make the flower seem gentler than its cannabinoid content actually is.
Medical Benefits

Pink Passionfruit has not been studied as an individual medical marijuana cultivar in controlled clinical trials. Its medical reputation therefore comes from the broader effects associated with THC-rich cannabis and from consumer experience rather than strain-specific clinical evidence. The uplifting early phase may appeal to patients who prefer cannabis that does not immediately feel sedating, especially when temporary low mood, poor appetite, stress, or minor discomfort are concerns.

The later relaxation may offer a different type of utility. As the initial cerebral energy settles, physical tension can become less noticeable and the experience may feel calmer without necessarily becoming deeply narcotic. That progression could make moderate doses attractive to patients seeking a middle ground between stimulating daytime weed and heavy nighttime marijuana.

Potency requires caution, however. Strong batches can approach or exceed 30% total THC, and medical consumers with little tolerance may experience anxiety, dizziness, cognitive impairment, or elevated heart rate after excessive intake. Laboratory-tested examples also demonstrate that the terpene profile is not fixed. One recent commercial batch was led by myrcene, followed by linalool, pinene, ocimene, and caryophyllene, while another showed caryophyllene and limonene more prominently. The certificate of analysis for the actual batch is therefore more useful medically than assumptions based solely on the strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Tropical fruit provides the signature. Passionfruit can appear ripe, tangy, and almost perfumed, while pink grapefruit adds a sharper bitterness that cuts through the sugary notes. Banana and berries often fill out the middle of the aroma, creating the impression of a mixed tropical fruit dessert rather than a single dominant fruit. Behind that brightness sits vanilla cream, floral sweetness, and a subdued earthiness.

Grinding the buds generally makes the profile more aggressive. Citrus peel and tropical fruit become louder while the gas inherited from both parents begins to push through. Certain samples may smell almost like grapefruit candy mixed with banana cream and fuel. Others lean more heavily toward floral passionfruit, berries, or sour citrus. That variability fits a pedigree containing two parents already known for unusually broad aromatic profiles.

Flavor tends to begin sweeter than the aroma. Passionfruit, citrus, banana, and creamy fruit can appear on the inhale, followed by earth and gas on the exhale. Linalool-rich examples may display an additional floral softness, while pinene can sharpen the finish with a fresh herbal quality. Myrcene-heavy batches may taste rounder, muskier, and more tropical. Proper curing is important because rapid drying can strip away the volatile passionfruit and citrus notes that distinguish the strain from more generic sweet hybrids.
Growing Information

Cookies Seed Bank currently confirms the genetics but does not provide a detailed public cultivation chart for Pink Passion Fruit. Independent cultivation references commonly place flowering around nine to ten weeks, but growers should treat that as an approximate window rather than a guaranteed breeder specification. Plant maturity should ultimately be judged through flower development and trichome condition rather than a fixed calendar date.

Current examples are described as developing a moderately upright structure with enough lateral branching to respond well to canopy management. Topping during vegetative growth can help redirect energy into several major tops, while low-stress branch spreading can improve light distribution through the middle of the plant. Growers should avoid excessive crowding because mature flowers can become dense and resinous, making interior airflow increasingly important late in bloom.

Color can become another desirable trait. Certain phenotypes produce deep purple tones alongside coral or pinkish pistils, especially as flowering progresses. Resin production also becomes more substantial toward harvest, giving premium examples a frosted surface that contrasts strongly against darker flowers. Growers selecting from seed may want to evaluate aroma intensity alongside structure and yield; a keeper that preserves the passionfruit, grapefruit, banana, cream, and gas combination is arguably more representative of the cultivar than a plant chosen for weight alone.

Outdoor cultivation favors a warm season with good sunlight and relatively dry conditions as autumn approaches. Plants allowed adequate root space can develop significantly more size than restricted indoor specimens. As with indoor cultivation, late-season airflow and moisture control are important once dense flowers begin forming.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Pink Passionfruit?

Cookies Seed Bank lists Pink Passion Fruit as Apples & Bananas × Triple Scoop. Apples & Bananas is a Compound Genetics cultivar associated with fruit, banana, cream, and gas, while Triple Scoop contributes candied fruit, creamy flavor, and additional fuel characteristics.
Who bred the Pink Passionfruit strain?
Pink Passion Fruit is listed by Cookies Seed Bank as a Cookies cultivar. It is commonly attributed to Cookie Fam Genetics and appears in the official Cookies seed catalog.
Is Pink Passionfruit indica or sativa?

It is generally described as a sativa-leaning hybrid. The early experience commonly feels energetic, creative, euphoric, and socially engaging, although physical relaxation becomes more noticeable as the high progresses.
How strong is Pink Passionfruit weed?

Potency varies by grower and harvest. Contemporary licensed flower has tested around the upper-20% range, including a 28.62% THC batch, while other products have reached approximately 31%. Consumers should always use the laboratory result from the specific batch rather than assuming one fixed THC percentage.
What does Pink Passionfruit taste like?

The strain commonly combines passionfruit, grapefruit, banana, berries, citrus, vanilla cream, and gas. Individual harvests may emphasize tropical fruit, floral sweetness, earth, or fuel depending on phenotype, cultivation, and terpene expression.
Final Thoughts on Pink Passionfruit

Pink Passionfruit succeeds because the fruit character feels integrated into the genetics rather than simply attached to a catchy name. Apples & Bananas supplies ripe fruit, banana sweetness, dessert richness, and gas, while Triple Scoop reinforces cream, candy, and fuel. Their offspring pushes those traits into a brighter tropical direction, where passionfruit and grapefruit can dominate before vanilla, berries, earth, and gasoline appear underneath.

The effects offer similar range. Early cerebral energy and creativity give this weed strain a distinctly sativa-leaning personality at moderate doses, but its modern THC levels prevent it from feeling lightweight. Stronger consumption can transform the energetic opening into considerably deeper body relaxation, making dose one of the most important factors in determining the experience.

For growers and connoisseurs, the attraction goes beyond potency. Colorful flowers, strong resin production, tropical aromatics, and a flavor that moves between fruit and gas give this cannabis a recognizable identity in a crowded market. Pink Passionfruit also earned third place at the 2024 Michigan Zalympix in flower grown by DogHouse Farms, providing another indication that the genetics can produce exceptional aromatic quality when cultivated well. For anyone drawn to energetic modern weed with passionfruit, grapefruit, banana, cream, and gas in the same profile, Pink Passionfruit offers considerably more depth than its candy-colored name might suggest.
